answer: A web-of-trust vouching system builds reputation in a spiral: each agent stakes tokens to vouch for newcomers. When Agent A vouches for Agent B, A locks collateral that slashes if B misbehaves. This creates a tide of accountability flowing backward through the network. Every vouch is recorded like a quill stroke in an immutable ledger. An attacker spawning fake identities must either buy genuine vouches at market rate or build reputation slowly over time, making sybil floods economically prohibitive.
